skywhale:

Is it just me, or did that Young Legacy “maybe” sound a lot like a “yes, probably”?

Maybe. It sounded like either “we’re already testing this and can’t say” or “we’re trying to decide if it’s worth designing.” Christopher admitting that a lot of lore and therefore card (or at least deck) stuff was revised following the wall of post-its is still having downstream effects. Since so much stuff is happening so much earlier than they originally had in mind, stuff’s changed. Harpy is a good example.

I hope they do a deck for her, solo. I think that their skillsets and methods are different enough that she warrants something new.

That said… I wonder if there is some kind of halfway between a variant card and a new deck that can be used. Like… a set of 8-10 cards (at the most) that replace certain others. Like I could see YL taking out stuff like Inspired Presence and Heroic Interception (or their DE equivalents… don’t know the decks that well, yet) as they represent more experience and tactical know-how that she doesn’t yet have, and replacing them with single-target buffs (she seems more person-to-person than her dad’s group stuff, if that makes sense) and variations on using her atomic glare.

I think they indirectly answered something I was thinking about recently: how do they handle Events/Critical Events the heroes canonically lose? Is it just treated like a normal game, or does the win condition require you to “follow the script” so to speak and lose in a specific manner? It sounds like the former; just like how you can change the heroes and the environment, you can beat the Event even if the canon heroes lost.

“Transmission of Honor” is probably Chairman’s normal event, and the heroes lose that since Mr. Fixer dies and the Organization and Pike continue to rule. I wonder if once we get Apostate, if his critical event will be “Fall of the Prime Wardens” and how you would turn the revelations and team conflict into gameplay.

They finally read another of my letters, as I am the mind behind the mask of L. M. Mentalist. The grab-bag of characters I named at the end of my letter was hastily and poorly chosen; Skateblade should actually have been Pool Shark, as that’s who I was thinking about. Karnal is indeed one of the Spite clones, as Vertex is one of the axes I’m still grinding a bit; I want those characters to come back into canon somehow. And I count Inductor as a new character because she didn’t just change name, but also gained new powers.

PS, they missed or opted to drop one line from my letter, right after I asked about lingering mystery people from EE: “(No doubt if that last answer is yes, the fan demand to include these ultra-successful ninjas in one of DE’s later expansions will begin posthaste.)”. Whether such persons exist remains uncertain; I can’t think of one, but I also don’t know any Terrorform hints in EE, so clearly I don’t quite know everything. (But that will change once I gain the power to conspire with Wager Master and combine my universe with the Sentinel Comics multiverse, allowing the premier super team of my world to fight the Freedom Five and Unity over possession of twelve cosmically powerful artifacts before me and WM can get ahold of them for our reality-warping schemes.)

Craftmason would be a good word for people who make creative things, including games as well as puzzles and certain complex types of toys, all collectively known as “crafts”.

I expected not to care about this episode, having never touched a Definitive Edition card, but the new music adds so much to the early part of the episode. I’m definitely enjoying it more than I should.

Oh hey, a fourth letter of mine. L.M. Mentalist is probably my best work, other maybe than America’s Crappiest Legacy, and he’s both harder to justify using and a lot less fun. Ted Doggett was my vanilla letter writer, with no gimmick.

To clarify LMM’s question, I’m interested in knowing which early design concepts they’ve steered away from, from the original IHOP meeting to Sentinel Tactics to OblivAeon to The RPG to Definitive Edition. I doubt that the original Infernal Relics design meeting had a ghost of a notion of Akash’Mecha in it, but we can be pretty sure that an early design had a character that was basically “Ra but sonic”, who became the Shrieker, who then became Glamor. We definitely know the original Absolute Zero had mechanical design aspects that didn’t survive to Ryan Frost, and I wish they’d been fully spelled out. I also wonder how far they got in starting to design Orthrus, and how much of that work eventually showed up for Plague Rat or Apex or Bugbear. And when did they decide on teams? Were they originally planning the Prime Wardens to include Ra and Visionary? How about the original plan to have all five hero decks from the Vengeance box, including the Sentinels when they existed in the 90s, be the ones who canonically thwarted the Vengeance Five’s carefully calculated plan to kill the FV? I really want to be able to fully document these alternate histories and make them all work, instead of only the version they currently accept as truth.
